note.note:
Consult Summary:
- Acute onset left arm weakness with facial tingling and dysphagia/speech difficulty; suspected stroke requiring emergency hospital evaluation; ambulance arranged to transport patient to local A&E; patient advised to keep front door unlocked; physician staying on the line during transport.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Woke about one hour ago with inability to move left arm; left facial tingling; speech becoming harder/slower; difficulty swallowing.
- Associated symptoms: Left facial tingling; dysphagia; speech changes.
- Negative/other systems: No left leg symptoms; no chest pain reported; no notable facial asymmetry noticed by patient.
- Onset/duration/progression: Symptoms began about one hour ago and persist.
- Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes; hypertension.
- Medications: Metformin; Losartan; Amlodipine.
- Allergies: Penicillin.
- Social history: Lives alone; former smoker; consumes alcohol on weekends (beers).
- Family history: Father with heart disease (unspecified details).
- Other: No one at home to assist; telephonic visit.

Examination:
- Not documented.

Impression:
- Working diagnosis: Suspected acute cerebrovascular event (stroke).

Plan:
- Ambulance dispatched to patient’s home; transport to local hospital A&E with stroke team assessment to determine possible treatment.
- Advise front door to be left unlocked; patient to sit in the hallway to facilitate access.
- Doctor to remain on the line until ambulance arrives to monitor and reassure patient.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements: vital signs; neuro/physical examination findings; last known well time; blood glucose; imaging results (CT/MRI) and stroke scale assessment; any contraindications or advanced directives; formal discharge/follow-up plan.
- Internal conflicts: None identified.
- Transcript quality: Clear telehealth encounter; some details limited by absence of visual assessment; overall comprehensible; no audio disturbances noted.
